newsitem.title: USA: CSCE to raise margins on coffee futures March 18.
newsitem.headline: CSCE to raise margins on coffee futures March 18.

text.p: The Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange (CSCE) said late Monday it will raise margins on its arabica coffee futures contracts, effective March 18.

"Until further notice, members shall require from customers who are members or members of the trade a minimum of $7,500 (includes $3,000 spot charge) for net long or short positions in the March 1997 coffee "C" contract and a $6,500 (includes $2,000 spot charge) for the net long or short positions in the May 1997 coffee "C" contract," exchange economist Raymond Wamser said in a statement.
The margin on all other coffee "C" contracts will be increased to $4,500, from $4,000.
The changes comes just two weeks after the exchange last raised the margins on all coffee "C" contracts.
In addition, straddle or arbitrage transactions will require a minimum of $1,500 for customers who are members or members of the trade.
The $3,000 spot charge for March 1997 and the $2,000 spot charge for May 1997 are applicable to all straddle and arbitrage transactions involving these months, the exchange said.
For customers who are not exchange members or a member of the trade, margins will be 140 percent above trade rates, CSCE said. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodities Desk, 212 859 1640))
